content.comment_body: I have an application called Triplex that I need to convert from another brand to [product_name]. Has anyone here done a similar conversion before? I've attached a sample program. Appreciate any help!

This appears to be a simple program, and it should be possible to implement it on [product_name]. Do you only have a printed or non-digital version of the original software? I haven’t personally converted from one software to another (like from Eaton easy to [product_name]), but I’m confident that the same functions exist in [product_name]. Sometimes, certain logic blocks behave differently across different brands, especially with more advanced features.

I don’t think it’s very difficult to recreate it in [product_name] software. You can build it in ladder, following exactly what’s described in your program copy. If ladder isn’t clear, you can convert it to FDB. A higher quality image would be useful, and it seems that some information is missing (for example, where is the T2 coil?). Additional pages would also help. Have you tried building it and encountered any issues?
Thanks for your response. It’s clear to me now that the conversion is possible. I’ve attached a screenshot of the example program.

Hello, Switch to the LAD Editor in [product_name] programming software (see the area marked in the image), and the program layout will look similar. Check the attachment. You’ll need to identify the addresses used in your original program and transfer them into [product_name]. Hope that helps.

Users generally agree that the process is manageable, especially for basic functions, provided the original program is fully documented. The main challenge mentioned involves missing information and potential differences in logic blocks between brands, but [product_name] software is highlighted as capable of replicating the needed logic and editor views.
